criteria.criterion: Central passenger service between Paddington low level/Paddington and Abbey Wood commenced by December 2018
required_elements: Crossrail/Elizabeth line central passenger service commenced
service was between Paddington low level/Paddington and Abbey Wood
criteria.promise_scope: Crossrail promised that services would commence in December 2018 in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood. Beneficiaries are passenger service users on that route; location is the central tunnel section from Paddington low level to Abbey Wood.
criteria.observed_scope: Evidence shows the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood later opened and operated as the Elizabeth line, with passengers using it on opening day; the route is specified, but the actual commencement date shown is 24 May 2022, not December 2018.
criteria.timing_requirement: By December 2018; the original undertaking states: "December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood".
criteria.explanation: Citation c1 documents the original timetable commitment. Citation c2 directly states that on 29 August 2018 the Crossrail Ltd Board decided instead to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019, showing the December 2018 opening would not occur. Citations c3 and c4 show the central passenger service on that route did in fact open and operate later as the Elizabeth line, including service between Paddington and Abbey Wood and passenger journeys on opening day. But those sources place the opening in 2022, not by December 2018.

trace.label: REFUTED
trace.verdict: The December 2018 opening commitment for the central passenger service between Paddington low level/Paddington and Abbey Wood is documented, but the evidence refutes that it opened by that date. Crossrail later deferred the opening, and the cited opening/operations evidence is for May 2022 rather than December 2018.
trace.reasoning:
Requested scope: Did London's Elizabeth line open its central passenger service from Paddington to Abbey Wood by the originally planned December 2018 date?

The original promise is specific: services in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood were to commence in December 2018 (c1). For the requested query, delivery requires both the correct route and commencement by that date. The evidence does show the route eventually opened as the Elizabeth line between Paddington and Abbey Wood and was carrying passengers on opening day (c3, c4). However, c2 directly records a board decision in August 2018 to open that central section in Autumn 2019 instead, which is incompatible with opening by the originally planned December 2018 date. The later service evidence confirms actual opening occurred after the promised date, so the exact time-bound commitment was not met.

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood”
https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/annual-update-on-crossrail-2017

c2: “The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018.”
https://tfl.gov.uk/corporate/transparency/freedom-of-information/foi-request-detail?referenceId=FOI-1470-1819

c3: “The Elizabeth line will operate 12 trains per hour between Paddington and Abbey Wood from Monday to Saturday 06:30 to 23:00.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-elizabeth-line-to-open-on-24-may-2022

c4: “The celebratory response to the opening saw around 260,000 journeys made on the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood across its opening day, clearly showing its popularity.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-celebrations-as-transformational-elizabeth-line-begins-operations
